studies.Title: Food, nutrient and heterocyclic amine intake and the risk of bladder cancer.
studies.Reference: Food, nutrient and heterocyclic amine intake and the risk of bladder cancer.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The association between diet and bladder cancer risk was evaluated among 912 incident bladder cancer cases and 873 controls in Spain.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: The association between diet and bladder cancer risk was evaluated among 912 incident bladder cancer cases and 873 controls in Spain.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Meat or fish intake, their cooking methods or level of doneness, or heterocyclic amine intakes were not significantly associated with risk. Intake of folate, other B-vitamins (B12, B6, B2) and retinol was also associated with a reduced risk, the strongest associations being for vitamin B6 (0.6 (0.4, 0.8) p trend=0.0006) and retinol (0.6 (0.4-0.9) p trend=0.004).
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: Intake of folate, other B-vitamins (B12, B6, B2) and retinol was also associated with a reduced risk, the strongest associations being for vitamin B6 (0.6 (0.4, 0.8) p trend=0.0006) and retinol (0.6 (0.4-0.9) p trend=0.004).
